$comment: Hatsu's decision matrix (zheref/hatsu#85, maintainer rulings of 2026-09-19). One row per condition a running workflow can stop on. `autonomous` rows are resolved by `default` with no question and each skill states the default in one line citing the row id; `ask-once-per-run` rows ask once through the surface's picker (Crazy Slots), seeded by `preferred`; `human-gate` rows are the gates canon reserves for the maintainer and cannot be reclassified by a consumer's own file. Validated by `nen schema check`; read by `nen stop --options` and by every skill before it asks. Rows cited by a skill's one-liner: dirty-tree (breath), cap-reached (en, sharingan, senkei, build), red-lint (kokusen, gyo), missing-focused-route (kokusen, tsukuyomi), missing-tool (hanten), release-precondition-red (getsuga), semantic-conflict (ao), mode-unknown (build), stale-base (ao), staging-flag and secret-shape (kokusen), unsettled-finding (hanten), release-go (mugetsu), canon-merge (getsuga), rewrite-published-history (aka), supply-chain-failure (hatsu-warmup), unruled-policy-surface (backlog-state), ambiguous-intent (rasengan), missing-argument and missing-configuration (every skill, WORKFLOW.md § 4 Ask, set up, continue). Data-only until a skill cites them: merge, mode-label, signing-material, on-device-act, missing-consumer-declaration (tenkai, once zheref/hatsu#83's engine grows the item).

rows.why: Ruling 2026-09-19: a dirty working copy at breath is always carried onto the new branch (stash including untracked, warm, restore). Nothing is discarded, the paths are listed in the report.

Ruling 2026-09-19: an owed reviewer round is requested on the maintainer's behalf while this PR's requested rounds are under nen/gates.json round_policy.maxRounds (never asked about); at maxRounds the run ends at not-ready with the board, never with a question. nen/workflow.json monitor.maxCycles is en's ACTING-cycle cap, a different number.

rows.default: hand the tree back to hatsu:rasengan with the failing check quoted
rows.why: Ruling 2026-09-19: a red iteration check kokusen cannot clear returns to rasengan; the turn continues. It is never a G5.

rows.default: hand the tree back to hatsu:rasengan to author the focused tests, then hatsu:tsukuyomi runs them
rows.why: Ruling 2026-09-19: a changed executable with no declared scoped lane gets its tests authored, never a stop and never the full suite as a substitute.

Ruling 2026-09-19: a missing tool or model id is installed or resolved through the surface's own catalogue probe, never with elevation and never a version the declaration did not pin. A verify-only row that cannot be installed is reported with its remedy line and the run continues where it can.
A base that can be fast-forwarded or merged mechanically is caught up; only a semantic conflict reaches semantic-conflict.

rows.default: nen changelog collate --write, then nen changelog completeness; reconcile in the same chunk and re-run nen release preflight
rows.why: Ruling 2026-09-19: a red release precondition (changelog completeness, uncollated fragments) is reconciled inside the same chunk of work, never a cause of stopping. An active RELEASE_HOLD and an open critical issue are not preconditions of this kind and stay human gates.

rows.default: skip ignored, large and out-of-scope paths; mention-or-skip an unmentioned deletion; commit local-config and binary paths only when the request named them
rows.why: Six of the seven nen stage triage flag kinds have a canon default; secret-shape is the seventh and is never askable (see secret-shape).

rows.default: hatsu:tenkai (apply, after its own diagnose) for a Hatsu-owned scaffolding piece

preferred.label: repair the scaffolding piece
preferred.command: scripts/tenkai_adopt.sh apply --repo <checkout>
preferred.consequence: the Hatsu-owned file is rendered; nothing routed to nen is written

preferred.label: assisted setup of the nen declaration
preferred.command: nen scaffold init --repo <checkout> --accept-detected --dry-run, then the real run after the questions are answered
preferred.consequence: the declaration lands as its own PR at G2 in a consumer repository

preferred.label: continue with the refusal quoted
preferred.command: nen shu <verb> --repo <checkout> --dry-run
preferred.consequence: the phase is reported not measurable here

rows.why: Ruling 2026-09-19: a missing declaration always gets a path forward. A Hatsu-owned scaffolding piece is repaired by tenkai without asking; a nen-routed declaration is set up through an assisted flow that asks the configuration questions itself and runs the owning verb.

rows.default: derive the value from the session, the branch, its open PRs and nen/workflow.json; one candidate a canon default covers is used and stated, otherwise ask with the candidates

preferred.label: use the derived value
preferred.command: re-run nen parse <skill> with the line completed by the derived value, then continue
preferred.consequence: the skill runs as if the value had been typed; the turn page names where it came from

preferred.label: use the next candidate
preferred.command: re-run nen parse <skill> with the line completed by the next candidate, then continue
preferred.consequence: the same run on the other reading

preferred.label: type the value
preferred.command: the picker's free-text answer completes the line; nen parse re-runs on it
preferred.consequence: nothing runs on a guess

rows.why: Ruling 2026-09-22: a missing or unparseable argument is completed inline, through the picker, and the operation continues; a refusal the maintainer has to retype around is never the outcome.

rows.default: set the item up in place through its owner, validate it with nen schema check, and resume the operation in the same turn

preferred.label: set it up now with the detected value
preferred.command: write the key through its owner (nen scaffold init, scripts/tenkai_adopt.sh apply, hatsu:jujutsu, or the file's own key), nen schema check, then resume
preferred.consequence: the configuration exists from now on; a tracked file rides this effort's branch or its own declaration PR at that repository's gate

preferred.label: set it up with another value
preferred.command: the same write with the value the maintainer picks or types
preferred.consequence: the same, on the maintainer's value

preferred.label: run once without it
preferred.command: the owning verb's --dry-run, or the phase reported not measurable here
preferred.consequence: nothing is written; the gap is named in Not delivered and asked again next time

rows.why: Ruling 2026-09-22: a missing configuration item is guided and written on the maintainer's behalf, then the operation continues. A skill aborts only when neither the agent nor the maintainer's answer can supply it: no tool or permission can, the value is a secret or signing material, or the act is on-device or a human gate.

preferred.label: Transmuter (machinery)
preferred.command: proceed in Transmuter mode
preferred.consequence: workflows, scripts, hooks, generators; G4 in a canon repository

preferred.label: Conjurer (canon and governance)
preferred.command: proceed in Conjurer mode
preferred.consequence: constitution, handbooks, skill prose; G4 in a canon repository

preferred.label: Enhancer (product code)
preferred.command: proceed in Enhancer mode
preferred.consequence: product source and tests; G2

rows.why: The mode is derived from the issue's labels and the diff's paths first; the picker fires only on a genuine tie.

preferred.label: take ours
preferred.command: git checkout --ours -- <path> && git add <path>
preferred.consequence: the branch's meaning wins on this hunk

preferred.label: take theirs
preferred.command: git checkout --theirs -- <path> && git add <path>
preferred.consequence: the base's meaning wins on this hunk

preferred.label: a genuine third resolution the run proposes
preferred.command: apply the shown patch, then git add <path>
preferred.consequence: both meanings are kept as the run describes

preferred.label: resolve it and show me the diff before anything is committed
preferred.command: resolve, then git diff --cached -- <path>; commit only after the maintainer reads it
preferred.consequence: the run types, the maintainer decides

rows.why: Ruling 2026-09-19: a semantic conflict in ao always goes to Crazy Slots with both sides shown verbatim and these four options; the run never picks a side.

preferred.label: extend scope and take the proposed fix
preferred.command: apply the reviewer's proposed fix
preferred.consequence: the change set grows by the finding

preferred.label: adopt the business rule the finding implies
preferred.command: record the rule in the PR body and apply it
preferred.consequence: a new rule, stated where it can be reviewed

preferred.label: keep the durable pending record and stop
preferred.command: hatsu:file with the finding as evidence
preferred.consequence: the finding outlives the branch as an issue

rows.why: hanten section 7: only after the four-fact test proves none of section 6's dispositions can be chosen without the maintainer.
CON-5: no agent in this plane merges main or its own PR anywhere.
CON-7: a merge in a canon repository decides how every other repository behaves.
CON-6: publication is the maintainer's recorded per-target go; no composite reaches it.
CON-4 and CON-25: the epic mode label and the building label are the maintainer's.
A force-push, a rewrite of a pushed commit, or an overwrite of a tracked path destroys somebody's history.
A secret-shape path is never committed and never askable: the answer is rotate or remove. Reported, not offered.
nen never synthesises signing material and neither does any skill; a missing identity ends the run naming the precondition.
A trust prompt or a security setting on a device is the maintainer's own act (jujutsu).
A checksum or manifest failure in the bootstrap is a security event the maintainer must see; never retried.
A consumer repository declaring a policy surface of its own is unruled; until ruled it is G2 and a genuine-looking exception is brought to the maintainer.

A request that is genuinely ambiguous, a scope change, or conflicting requirements canon does not adjudicate cannot be defaulted; rasengan brings it to the maintainer once, through Crazy Slots, with the readings it can see as the options.

preferred.label: the narrowest reading
preferred.command: proceed with the reading the run states, recorded on the turn page
preferred.consequence: the smallest change that satisfies the request as read

preferred.label: the wider reading
preferred.command: proceed with the wider reading the run states
preferred.consequence: more surface changes; named in the PR body

preferred.label: restate the request
preferred.command: stop; the maintainer restates
preferred.consequence: nothing authored on a guess
